[0:00 to 0:20] Hi, I'm Gio. I built an AI-native ATS: role setup, CV parsing and a pipeline, plus one twist called Beyond the Scan. I'll show it working, then how it's built, why it's built this way, and what I'd do next.

[0:20 to 0:50] Blocks 1 to 3 are the must-haves from the brief and all work end to end. Block 4 is the twist. Stack: React, Vite and TypeScript; FastAPI and SQLite; OpenAI structured outputs. OpenAI is mocked in all 119 tests, so they're free and run in under a second.

[0:50 to 1:40] Before choosing the twist I ran a short discovery interview. Tim and Chris role-played recruiters. I asked about their last hire, what makes them reject someone in 30 seconds, and the one thing they'd fix. The answer that stood out was the 15 to 20 seconds on the last 2 jobs. I treat all of this as a hypothesis, not proof.

[1:40 to 2:10] This is the shortcut the whole feature is built around. OVI's Milo already reads and scores every CV, so 'read the other 900' isn't my twist. What's left after AI has read everything is human attention.

[2:10 to 7:00 (live, about 5 min)] Switch to the app. Before the talk: stop the backend, move backend/ats.db aside so the app starts empty, restart. 1) New role: paste sample_data/demo/job_description.txt (about 8 s). Point out the must-haves and 'Not used for screening: Preferred age 25 to 35'. 2) Upload CVs: select all 9 PDFs in sample_data/demo/cvs (about 35 s, 3 at a time). Talk over it: 2 AI calls per CV, duplicates caught before any AI call. 3) Open Layla: timeline, years counted in code, contact links. Move her to Shortlisted. 4) Scan mode: reject James, no interruption. Skip to Priya: amber note, job 4 of 5. Reject: the check quotes her Python and SQL work. Look again, then move her to Interview. If the AI or Wi-Fi fails: cd backend && uv run python reset_demo.py loads the same 9 CVs instantly.

[7:00 to 7:30] The bullets are labelled duty, action or outcome, because Tim's second reject reason was 'did they actually contribute value?'. Outcomes are labelled as claimed in the CV, not verified.

[7:30 to 8:00] The wording is neutral: it doesn't question the recruiter's reason, because presentation, seniority and fit are legitimate reasons. It just shows what isn't on the card. In the demo, 2 of 10 candidates trigger it.

[8:00 to 9:45] All prompts live in backend/prompts.py and each is paired with a Pydantic schema, so the model must answer in that exact JSON shape. Plain-code modules: cvs.py reads PDFs and counts years; evidence.py verifies quotes and decides whether evidence is buried. About 2 AI calls per CV, well under a cent each.

[9:45 to 11:15] LLMs are unreliable at arithmetic and can invent text, so anything that has to be exact is done in code. The AI proposes, code checks. If a quote can't be found in the right job's section, it's shown as unverified and can't interrupt the recruiter.

[11:15 to 13:00] Three tables. The decisions table only ever gets new rows, so history is never rewritten. Each prompt has a few rules that came from testing: the discriminatory-criteria rule, ignoring instructions inside CVs, and never letting the AI judge years.

[13:00 to 14:45] The brief asks what I skipped and why. The biggest one: no scoring, because Milo already does it. My first idea was an algorithm that learns from swipes; I dropped it because it learns bias, like Amazon's 2018 hiring model, and hiring AI is high-risk under the EU AI Act. UPDATE the 'Check runs in Scan mode' card if the board check gets built.

[14:45 to 16:30] The demo CVs were written to trigger the check, so they prove the mechanism, not the value. The scan-gap rate on real CVs is unknown, and that's the first thing to measure. Speed: an upload takes about 13 seconds with the extra evidence call.
[16:30 to 18:00] Being explicit about what it doesn't solve. Volume is Milo's job. Excel and channel chaos need integrations, which is the next slide.

[18:00 to 19:30] Validate before expanding. If recruiters don't find the check useful on real CVs, nothing else on this slide matters. Then connect it to Milo so it isn't a second evidence engine. The intake ideas come from the interview: Excel, scattered channels and an accidental LinkedIn auto-reject.
[19:30 to 20:00] Close on the one line. Then questions.
